question: All people have their rights, but it is better for all of us that different sorts of people should keep to their own kind.
essay:
**Disagree.**

The idea that “different sorts of people should keep to their own kind” is harmful because it treats human difference as a reason for separation rather than cooperation. All people do have rights, and those rights include the freedom to live, work, and associate with others without being sorted into rigid categories. A society works best when people are judged as individuals, not reduced to race, religion, class, ethnicity, or any other label.

Keeping people apart does not create peace; it usually creates fear, misunderstanding, and unfairness. When groups are isolated from one another, stereotypes grow stronger and trust becomes harder to build. On the other hand, when people of different backgrounds interact, they are more likely to develop respect and common purpose. Diversity is not a threat to society—it is one of the things that can make society stronger, more adaptable, and more humane.

A fair society should protect everyone’s rights equally while encouraging people to live together with mutual respect. We do not need to keep people “to their own kind” to preserve order. We need shared rules, equal treatment, and the recognition that our differences do not make us less deserving of dignity.
label: Strongly disagree
